In the not too distant past music roots were pretty much a cut and dried thing "Believe It" by Tony Williams is music seek an all new level. FANCY DANCER — Bobbi Humphrey — Blue Note BNLA 550-G — Producer: Larry Mizel! and Chuck Davis — List: 6.98 A Bobbi Humphrey album is more than music and songs. It is a total concept of interaction between musician and music. There is no excess and there is no self indulgence. On “Fancy Dan- cer” Humphrey's flute and vocal runs move easi- ly through the spaces of jazz and progressive soul in a manner unobtrusive and smooth Fills and bridges are handled with care while a rhythmic base sets off the running mood of the music Top cuts include "Sweeter Than Sugar" and "You Make Me Feel So Good " "Fancy Dancer" by Bobbi Humphrey is the musical light fantastic. LIFE IS BEAUTIFUL — Tony Bennett — Improv 7112 - List: 6.98 Tony Bennett's vocal strength carries with it a sense of softness and tenderness that surfaces just often enough on "Life Is Beautiful” to make this series of songs a natural in the realm of easy listen. Simple ballads and love songs take on a humanistic tone of dimension that transcends mere music to something special Top cuts in- clude "Life Is Beautiful," "I Used To Be Color Blind" and "As Time Goes By ” "Life Is Beau- tiful” by Tony Bennett is music nurtured by something that is alive and well in all of us SOUNDTRACK FROM THE MOVIE MAHOGANY - Diana Ross - Motown M6-858S1 - Producer: Michael Masseer - List: 6.98 True to the superior quality of movie sound- tracks in recent years the musical backdrop to the movie "Mahogany" works on two levels of comprehension The music remains true to the undulating emotional dips of the movie while the overall care in production makes it a collection of music just as valid on its own Top listens include "Can You Hear It In My Music." "Let's Go Back To Day One" and "You Don't Have To Be Alone.” The music from “Mahogany" strikes the right musical vessel. MAKE ME FEEL LIKE A WOMAN - Jackie Moore - Kayvette 801 — Producer: Brad Shapiro - List: 6.98 Jackie Moore is a practitioner of a musical form that's been around for quite a while Her in- terpretation of the time-honored blues torch singer stance is a perfect reflection on a form that appears to have staying power "Make Me Feel Like A Woman" showcases her talents at their finest as her vocal outpourings and a taut instrumental backing make the rounds of the traditional as well as the upbeat Top cuts in- clude "At The Top Of The Hill" and "The Bridge That Lies Between Us " "Make Me Feel Like A Woman" gets down on yoursoul. SLEEP WARM - Rod McKuen - Warner Bros. BS 2889 - Producer: Rod McKuen & Wade Alex- ander - List: 6.98 Rod McKuen's interpretation of story and song is one we all aspire to His gruff vocal quality proves almost romantic in its simplistic tones and makes for an interesting music presentation. The form continues on "Sleep Warm" as his exposi- tion of the old and new in pop cut a fine path through melody and arrangement Top listens in- clude "Will You Love Me Tomorrow?" "Since You Asked" and "You Are The Sunshine Of My Life " "Sleep Warm" by Rod McKuen is the positive half light of day in a musical night The ti- tle says it all. r 28 November 1 . 1975

The group is shown above performing a number for an upcoming appearance on Don Cornelius' Soul Train. From left to right are: Henry Fambrough, Billy Henderson, Bobby Smith, Phillipe Wynne and Pervis Jackson. Currently the Spinners are hot on the charts with their single and LP, “Games People Play," and "Pick Of The Litter." soul waves WSID Baltimore (Black Gold) and WLPL-FM have acquired four new station personnel of late. New account executives are Sherry Berman, who comes to the station after being area promotion manager for Stewart’s Dept, stores; Oswald Copeland, who's experience in radio includes working at CBS Guiana for eight years; and Brock Abernathy, who was formerly employed at WYNG Goldsboro, N.C. as sales manager. Dee Mack has been appointed sales manager, joining the station after nine years as media supervisor of W.B. Doner, Baltimore. Sonny Taylor, PD at WWRL. N.Y. reported the Latin sound is really catching on in his area, especially in the case of Eddie Drennon’s "Let’s Do The Latin Hustle" on the Friends & Co. label. The trend's popularity is causing problems, though; the cover version by the Young Sisters on Philips is so similar in instrumentation and phrasing that consumers may not be able to tell the difference. Nevertheless, WWRL will stick to playing the original (Drennon wrote the tune), despite the confusion, following the same policy implemented with "When You're Young And In Love"; quoting Sonny, "WWRL will not play two versions of the same song. Bermie McCain, WHAT Phila. , reports the change to a 90% album play format has led to a change of duties. All shifts have been cut to three hours, necessitating Bernie’s return to the air "It’s an unusual feeling to be back," he said, “you work so long to get off the air." Bernie’s finding the airshift "an interesting challenge” helping him “to re- member and understand the difficulties facing his air crew.” This change is temporary; Bernies filling in until he locates the ideal person. 'Til be scrupulous in choosing," he said, “but I’m willing to fire me anytime." Despite the format change, WHAT’s personnel has remained stable. Bernie honestly explained that many have expressed objections, "nobody ever seems to be happy with a change, but your personality in music changes quickly." He feels that once initial adjustments are made, the jocks will be able to use their greater freedom of choice creatively, suiting station personality to playlist. Getting to music, sounds happening in Philly on WHAT include new albums by Aretha, Dionne Warwicke, The Commodores, Bill Withers and Jackie Wilson, and The Chi-Lites. Lesser known artists who are making an impression are A! Jarreau, Jon Lu- cien and Esther Satterfield, with her new LPon A&M called "Once I Loved." Harry Jeffery, PD at WOOK radio in D C. was enthusiastic over the success of the First Annual Motorcycle Parade, sponsored by the station through the Chuck Long Trike & Cycle Club. Horseman, cyclist and skydiver Chuck, WOOK’s nighttime jock, has long been heavily involved in community road safety with the club. In terms of turnout, this seems the best reward for his efforts thus far. From Atlanta, Philadelphia, Baltimore and scattered regions, unnamed came 2,000 motorcycles. End to end, they stretched two miles, that’s 40 blocks, wrecking havoc on Washington, D C. traffic. No grudges held, though The Horse Farm picnic that followed drew nearly 8,000 to free food provided by WOOK and local contributors, and things are already set for next year. Bill Moon, program director at WVKO called in to say that they have had some staff changes and the new WVKO lineup includes: Roshan Vance from 6 a m. to 10 a.m., and K.C. Jones from 1 0 a.m. to 3 p m. Eric Stone, "the Rock," entertains the kids after school from 3 p.m. to 7 p m. with Carl Conner handling the evening mike from 7 p.m. to midnight. Mike Hudson is graveyard jock from midnight to six. . . . E. Rodney Jones, the mam man at WVON in Chicago said the tunes that are making the most noise his way are Quincy Jones’ "Is It Love That We’re Missin’," "I’m In Heaven,” by Touch of Class, "I’m On Fire," by Jim Gilstrap, "Pearly Whites," by Jimmy Witherspoon, Sister Sledge's "Love Has Found Me" and "Go On And Dream" by Johnny Bristol. Rodney also added that the LPs burning up the Chicago charts are the Spinners’ "Games People Play,” "I Get High On You," Sly Stone, “2nd Anniversary," Gladys Knight and the Pips, The "Mahogany" soundtrack featuring Diana Ross, and "Drama V" by the Dramatics. Don Mac, the music director over at KDAY in L A. said the new additions to their playlist for this week include Al Green's "Full Of Fire," David Ruffin's "Walk Away From Love," "School Boy Crush," by AWB, "Love Rollercoaster," by the Ohio Players and "Superbad, Superslick," by James Brown. Don also added that new Bobby Womack LP on UA “Safety Zone," featuring Herbie Hancock and the Pointer Sisters is a killer Bobby Elliott down at KNOK said his new additions for this week will be "Blind Over You," Chicago Gangsters, "Roll With The Punches," Groundhog, "Full Of Fire," AI Green, “You’ve Got Style,” Phil Upchurch, "It’s Alright (This Feeling)" by the Notations, and "Get Out Of My Life, " by Tommy Young. Randy Sterling the mellow man who plays the latest soulful tunes called in to say that KGBC is preparing for its annual Halloween contest. The radio station distributes cards amongst the local elementary school children who fill in their names and return them to the station After the kids finish trick or treating on Halloween the stations at 7:30 p m will draw cards and the winners will receive bicycles, footballs, baseballs, athletic uniforms and records. Randy also said that the hot ones down in south Texas are: “Let's Do It Again." Staple Singers, "Shotgun Shuffle," The Sunshine BAND, To Each His Own," Faith, Hope & Charity, "That’s The Way I Like It,” K C and the Sunshine Band and "It Only Takes A Minute," by Tavares. cashbox/news United Artists Hits Hottest Sales Month Ever In October HOLLYWOOD — United Artists Records "Necessity was the mother of our suc- cess." said Henry Stone, who runs the T K operation in Miami and is one of the genuine success stories of the year With K.C and the Sunshine Band, George McCrae, Jackie Moore, Latimore, Gwen McCrae, Jimmy "Bo" Horne, Clarence Reid, Little Beaver, Timmy Thomas and King Floyd burning up the charts, now Stone has cause to bless the phone call he received some years ago That was when he was told that Elektra. Atlantic and Warner Bros, would be pulled from his distributorship - Tone Dist. in Hialeah — and WEA was to be formed It meant that Stone decided to put his ears really on the marketplace For years as a distributor he had often found him- self calling a major to turn them on to a fast breaking, and usually soul, single on oneof the smaller labels he handled. Why not do it for himself? Stone did — with enormous success as T K s first year of operation has seen him establishing Hialeah and Miami as the spot that's hot And more K.C. and the Sunshine Band are on T K Records but Stone has established a working pattern of dis- tributing that has, for example, King Floyd on Chimneyville Records, Jackie Moore of Kayvette, Latimore on Glades, Clarence Reid on Alston and more Wilson Pickett and Frederick Knight are now associated with Stone bringing theirown labels into his fertile field. "I knew we had the atmosphere down in Miami."' says’ Stone "A family at- mosphere with productive musicians and excellent producers. The record busi- ness needs independents and I'll make a deal with anybody who feels they can produce hits.” That's Henry and the Family Stone. Durkin will have overall responsibility for providing ad- ministrative services to the Columbia, Epic and CBS custom label a&r depart- ments. His functions will include the pre- paration and monitoring of all a&r and re- cording budgets, the coordination and scheduling of all single and album product, the periodic review of the con- tractual and product status of each artist on the labels, and maintenance of the studio recording schedule. Durkin will also be responsible for the copyright ad- ministration department and work with business affairs in areas related to artist contracts. Durkin most recently served as direc- tor of a&r administration for CBS Records, and has been manager of Columbia Record's a&r administration Warner Record Group: Most Successful Sept, Hot Qtr NEW YORK — The Warner Communica- tions Record Group, which includes Atlantic, Warner Bros, and Elektra/- Asylum, has just completed one of its most successful quarters in its history, according to Steven J. Ross, chairman of Warner Communications. September was the best month ever for the company, he added with figures over $31 ,000,000. Consolidated revenues for the third quarter were $82,253,000 from $78,644,000 in the third quarter of 1974 Profits for the third quarter totalled $14,594,000 compared to the 1974 total of $13,158,000 Operating revenues showed a slight increase for the first nine months of 1975; $221,423,000 over the nine months in 1974 total of $211,114,000 Income from operating units dropped in the first nine months to $34,530,000. The total in the period of 1974 was $34,959,000 Commented Ross: "Domestic records, international records and music publish- ing all showed gains over last year. Our recorded music and music publishing division had the best quarter in its history in both sales and earnings.” The strong showings for the third quarter reflect the success of Warner Records Music Group product from the Eagles, America, Average White Band, Marshall Tucker Band. Linda Ronstadt, Bad Company, Spinners, Richard Pryor, Allman Brothers, Graham Central Sta- tion. James Taylor, Orleans, Rod Stewart, Jethro Tull, Black Sabbath, Bee Gees and Fleetwood Mac The music group includes apart from the above Labels, Reprise, Atco, WEA International and WB Music. The parent company Warner Com- munications also returned a record net income and earnings per share for the third quarter of this year. Net income was $12,512,000, above the $12,344,000 figure for 1974's third quarter. There was, however, a decline in revenues to $165,839,000 from last year's record total of $192,273,000. Ful- ly diluted earnings per share rose to $0 73 against $0.61 a year ago. Earnings per share showed a greater percentage income as a result of the continuing re- duction in shares outstanding. The average number of fully diluted shares outstanding during the third quarter of 1975 was $17,243,000 compared to 20,544,000 in 1974 Revenues for the first nine months of 1975 were $491,807,000 against $545,137,000 in the same period of 1974. Earnings per share rose to $2.24 from $2.04. Ross, in his statement accompanying the figures stated that film revenues and pre-tax income were below last year's re- sults. television distribution profit showed a strong advance, WCI's publishing (books) operated profitably during the quarter although below last year's level, with the overall division showing a loss due to the company's re- maining foreign publishing company. Arista Sales & Profits ‘Over 700 Percent Increase In 1st Quarter NEW YORK — Arista Records sales and profits for the first quarter of their fiscal year — three months ending Sept. 30 — were "up more than 700 percent over the same period the previous year" re- ported Elliot Goldman, executive vice president of the label. Success of the first quarter was at- tributed by Goldman to sales of the Outlaws debut album — “now at 350,000 units," he stated, and also the album and single from the U K group, Bay City Rollers, "Saturday Night." Also making impact during this period was product from Barry Manilow, Melissa Man- chester, Tony Orlando and Dawn, and the "Funny Lady" soundtrack. Goldman stated that Arista's "unprec- edented first year success has continued and is already being surpassed by the ex- traordinary sales activity generated so far this year. We have also felt an enormous reaction to the release of five new albums.” Albums cited by Goldman are from Barry Manilow, Gil Scott-Heron, Eric Carmen, Terry Garthwaite, Tony Orlando and Dawn 30% 1 st Quarter Increase For Screen Gems — Columbia Durkin NEW YORK — Screen Gems-Columbia Music, the publishing arm of Columbia Pictures, has reported a 30 percent in- crease in recording activity for the first quarter of fiscal 1976, according to Irwin Z. Robinson, vice president and general manager. Currently the company has product in- volving Helen Reddy, Gladys Knight and the Pips, Diana Ross, Jeff Perry, and Anne Murray. Robinson stated that the increase reflected activity on all fronts — pop, country, r&b and special album packages and films. The recent acquisition of the Press Music catalog — containing the "Another Somebody Done Somebody Wrong Song" — is already being reflect- ed and 1 7 of the company's songs are in- cluded in the QMC television package, "Neil Sedaka's Greatest Hits." Another 17 Screen Gems-Columbia titles will be featured in the upcoming "Tony Orlando For Columbia House" a TV package. Copyright, Piracy Court Activity NEW YORK — Copyright and anti-piracy activity include court action in Atlanta and Milwaukee last week. Three writer members and 30 publisher members of ASCAP have filed two lawsuits in federal court in Atlanta against Harry W. Farmer, president of the Omnibus Group. Inc., an Atlanta-based corporation. The plaintiffs allege in their suits that their copyrighted songs were performed unlawfully over radio stations WAXY of Waycross, Ga., and WBLU of Salem, Va , both operated by Omnibus and its subsidiaries. Effort Planned NEW YORK — "The Leslie West Band." the guitarist’s second solo effort on Phantom Records, will be the subject of a strong nationwide merchandising cam- paign with release this week. A two-pronged sales program will cov- er the east and west coasts. The Wherehouse chain in California will in- clude the LP in a promotion backed with radio time buy. Sam Goody's will spotlight the album as part of a television package covering New York and Philadelphia, featuring 90 TV and radio spots the week of Nov. 29. Trade advertising and a prepared radio spot complete the cam- paign. West's band is currently on nationwide tour. Fantasy ‘Twofer’ LPs Latest Prestige Releases BERKELEY — Fantasy Records have re- leased five new Prestige "twofers” in- cluding sets by John Coltrane. Miles Davis, Eric Dolphy and Ron Carter, Il- linois Jacquet and Mose Allison, bring- ing to 1 05 the total number of two-record sets released in the series. The an- nouncement of the new releases was made by Ralph Kaffel. president of Fan- tasy/Prestige/Milestone. The concept of twofers, repackaged and remastered double LP sets of older classic recordings, originated at the Berkeley-based label. The new releases are being supplemented by a full array of four-color posters, including one for the late Cannonball Adderleys epic work about John Henry, "Big Man."’ The twofers are, additionally, fully annotated and re-designed in packaging, with a full program of material being supplied to distributors and retailers. "Magic" is a reissue of "Where?" Ron Carter's first album as a leader, and "Far Cry” a 1960 Eric Dolphy LP The LP features contributions from distin- guished sidemen Booker Little. Jaki Byard, Mai Waldron and George Duvi- vier "Dig" is Miles Davis’ fifth "twofer” con- taining his earliest recordings for the label, including his first recorded meet- ing with Sonny Rollins and a rare date with Al Cohn and Zoot Sims. Others ap-, pearing on the LP are John Lewis, Jackie McLean, Kenny Clarke, Art Blakey and Percy Heath. "The Stardust Session" by John Coltrane is an album that "Trane re- corded in one day, although the sides were previously only available as three separate LPs The quintet, including a Miles Davis rhythm section make the set an important chronicle in the life of John Coltrane. “How High The Moon” by Illinois Jac- quet, considered to be among the most formidable of jazz saxophonists, displays the rare emotionality that brought him in- to the company of Lionel Hampton, Count Basie, and his immortal Jazz at the Philharmonic concerts. WBS 81 57) Woman Tonight (2:19) (WB—ASCAP) (Peck) When you lay the needle to this record, don't walk away to pour yourself a drink — by the time the voices begin you may be apt to spill it. Instead of the expected, the boys dash off some good new-fashioned change. Healthy for all concerned and George Martin’s influence doesn't hurt a bit. Flip: No info, available. cashboxR&Bnewsreport r&b ingredients A few of the Ohio Players dropped by the office last week before their big gig at the Forum. Satch, Sugar and Marshall, who have had three gold LPs on Mercury this year, came by Cash Box to chat. The Players’ trip is to grow musically with every record they do. The three guys agreed that you have to grow into a new groove all the time. Sugar said, "If I don't grow. I don't change, and if I don't change, I don't grow. I want to stay in the mainstream of the musical scene and to do so I feel that we, as a group, have to explore and get into new areas of sound all the time.' 1 I asked Satch what "Sweet Sticky Thing" meant. “It's a story of a very old man in love with a very young girl he desires." We all cracked up at that. Satch is serious about his music. "I believe in telling people what's on my mind and being able to relate to them I have to be 100% true to myself.” "Love Rollercoaster,” their latest single is the story of the times they spent touring in Europe. Marshall said, "It was a happy experience being in Europe and going here and there. It was like being on a rollercoaster. That's how we got the light, happy flavor for the tune." Satch told us, "We keep fooling everybody all the time because they think they can put us in a mold Last year we were king of the discos and people thought that was all we could do. however we came out with a new concept and a whole new approach. We're into sexy music and we enjoy making music about love." Mercury Records also threw a lovely bash at the Beverly Hills Hotel for the Players last week. One of the interesting ladies there was the cover girl for the LP "Honey." The lovely lady is named Ester Cordet and she hails from San Diego. One interesting side note Ester told me occurred when they were shooting the inside cover. Ester was placed on a plexiglass sheet and was covered from head to toe with honey. "Well there was so much honey on me that the lights caused me to stick to the glass. In or- der to get me off the plexiglass they had to run hot water all over me." Caught the amazing Mr. Bobby “Blue” Bland at the Grove last week He was sensa- tional as his pure blues voice made a whole lot of witnesses out of the audience. By the way his new LP on ABC "Get On Down With Bobby Bland" is a monster . George Greif, personal manager for Barry White, Lament Dozier and the Crusaders will be making his acting debut in the Mark Rydell film "Harry And Walter Go To New York", currently shooting at the Burbank Studios. The film stars James Caan, Elliot Gould and Michael Caine. Greif will portray a safecracker in the Tony Bill-Don Devlin-Harry Gittes production . . . It will be released shortly . . . RAMSEY ON BOARD — Shown above is Ramsey Lewis when he and his group made a recent appearance on Soul Train The group is shown performing their latest single on Columbia "What The Name Of This Funk (Spider Man)'' off his new LP "Don’t It Feel Good " Edwin Starr, currently on the charts with "Stay With Me," just recently returned from an eight week tour of South Africa. Edwin called in to say that the trip was truly incredible because he felt he made some racial progress in that country when he. Betty Wright and Arthur Conley refused to perform in Durban after they learned that black Africans wouldn't be allowed to see their show. "We just refused to go on and the promoter gave us 500 free tickets for our African brothers and sisters. One of the problems down there is that the blacks live so far away from town it makes it difficult for them to see shows What people did was bring their clothes and food, etc to town that day and just stayed for the show The response was great. I got a chance to talk with a lot of younger white South Africans. They don't have the same views as the older generation and I see the situation maybe getting better all the time. I want to go back there real soon because I think it helps the blacks down there to see other blacks doing something rewarding with their lives and not thinking that there is no hope They don't have television in South Africa, so live shows are very important to the people." Edwin will be at the Starwood Nov. 6. Another hit tune for Edwin off his "Free To Be Myself” LP on Granite is "Abyssinia Jones." This one really shows off Edwin's great voice. The 21st Century who record for RCA will be releasing their next single very soon. The title will be "Does You Momma Know About Me?" I called Hamish to check it out and he reconfirmed that the group did the show Saturday and performed "School Boy Crush," "Cut The Cake" and "Person To Person ." Hamish said that Soul Train is one of their favorite American shows and that the group has been wanting to do the show since 1972. “However, we had a problem with our work permits which only allowed us to do two television shows So we did Midnight Special and Rock Concert I don't understand the whole thing, but probably somebody out there doesn't like us and has it in for us. The show will be on in a couple of weeks. Ernest James, program director at WBMX dislikes tight playlists because he always feels that there are enough quality records out there to make for good programming. Ernest is more into quality programming rather than tight playlists. "There is so much music available, and not just adequate material that I don't see any reason for a tight playlist," he said. "Also, LPs today have to be given tremendous consideration to your format My concept of a music station is to entertain, just like when you go to the mov- ies or a play I try to make WBMX have a sound that has variety, because good music is tight in quality." Steve Crumbley at WORL in Orlando feels tight playlists are nothing more than bad programming "When you stick to a tight playlist you first confine your jock from at- taining his true personality on the air and second your sound becomes machine oriented. Today people want more music, and there is so much good music out there, it would be criminal to play a few hits. The days of the top 20 or 30 are about over — we're going into a new age." Jim Maddox, pd over at KDAY feels that it's more important how you use your playlist rather than its length “It's no good to play the same records over and over again unless you can inject something else into it such as oldies and LP cuts. Jim also It is also very important how you expose your hit records. Hit records have to be played but you must be knowledgeable in your rotation to make sure they get the proper exposure without burning them out too soon The amount of records played is not that significant, but more importantly is how you are using them, " he said. Keith Adams at KDIA likes the tight playlist and finds it a necessary evil in order to compete “It’s evil in the fact that a lot of records never get exposed, however by sticking to our list it makes us competitive in our market Personally I don't think I have a good ear for picking hits, and in my opinion I feel that there aren't many guys out there today who can ” Keith also said he didn't think the tight playlist was good for the whole industry because stations with long lists are needed. "However there are such things as ratings and people today don't listen to the radio for long periods of time, usually they listen for 15 minutes or so periodically during the day, and when they listen they want to hear hits, so we play 25 singles, however they are the hits people want to hear. " Joe Fischer at WCKO doesn't believe in tight playlists. "There are 22 radio stations in our market including nine rockers and if we don't play a variety of records our sta- tion is no different than the others The only records that we repeat are in the top 20. however we add four or five records each week. Black radio especially shouldn't get into the tight playlist thing, because the young black artists need a chance to expose their product. I feel it's our job to expose and give our listeners more of a variety of music and at least let them hear what’s happening. We have separate disco hours that expose a lot of records which I think help open the door to explore new tunes and sounds. I'm for giving product exposure to see what happens with it.” J.D. Black, pd at KOKY said that they have a tight playlist. He laughed when he said "we let everybody bust them and then play the hits J.D. said tight playlists might be bad for the record companies and artists, however in his situation the tight playlist is better for his demographics. "Usually we have hit-bound records and the ones that become hits do so, however the mediocre records or marginal records will go sour, which makes it tough on the artist, but I feel that's what the record business is all about.” Al Parker over at WUFO doesn't like tight playlists at all. "When you use a tight playlist it makes your music too predictable, and I like to keep the listeners guessing. I like to be creative with the music because I feel you can do a better show Also I like open request lines so listeners can call up and give a request and know that it will go on in a while. With a tight playlist you might hear it three hours later in most cases." Al also doesn't like tight playlists because they don't give the lesser unknowns a chance. "Every week there are at least 20 established artists on the charts, and if you stick with them, newcomers would never get a shot I like a loose playlist so you can pick your music and be creative and spontaneous with yoursound Jimmy Stevens, WABQ, Cleveland — "No way a very tight playlist could work in the Cleveland market, as far as I can see The listeners are receptive to new sounds, in fact, they always anticipate something different from the station. With the amount of good music that's being put out today, a small playlist would not allow us to play what people want to hear." WABQ plays 40 records, along with 15 albums, with no restrictions on the cuts played There is no fixed rotation, allowing jocks reasonable freedom in what they play, and leaving the request line open and operative Says Jimmy “It all comes down to why you listen to radio; to hear things you already know of pick up on things you might not have heard Whatever the answer, WABQ's format has picked up in the ratings. Chuck Harris, WSRC, Durham — “With tight playlists, I don't feel the broadcasting industry is giving people on the upstart a fair shot I’m not suggesting a playlist be flooded with five or six unknowns, but staying strictly with superstar recorders doesn’t seem very realistic to me, since the superstars had to be up-and-comings once too. Somebody somewhere has to break a record I like having the freedom to give a good record by a new artist a try " WSRC is a 100% black station playing 40 records. Chuck feels the latitude afforded by the list helps the station with top 40 stations in the market jess levitt/phil dimauro 28 November8, 1975

To date almost two hundred versions of Weatherly's songs have been re- corded including ' Neither One Of Us.'' "You're The Best Thing That Ever Hap- pened To Me," "Midnight Train To Georgia' and "Where Peaceful Waters Flow. ” Shown, from left: attorney Owen I Sloane and Keca Music president (also | Weatherly's manager) Larry Gordon; Weatherly; ABC Records Chairman j Jerold H Rubinstein. June Pointer Quits Sisters For Health HOLLYWOOD — June Pointer has re- tired from live performances with The Pointer Sisters, including concerts and television for reasons of extreme mental and physical exhaustion, at the instruc- tion of her doctor, according to the Sis- ters' manager, David Rubinson. If health permits, she may resume re- cording and writing with the group in the future June's final engagement with the group was their three-day stint at the Cir- cle Star Theatre in San Carlos, Calif The Pointer Sisters are taping a guest appearance on the Carol Burnett Show this week. In addition to one-nighters around the country the next few weeks, they have three major engagements scheduled; New York's Bottom Line. November 19-23; Bimbo s in San Fran- cisco, November 26-29 and The Roxy in Los Angeles. December 2-7 With these engagements, the group returns to a more intimate setting, bring- ing a new cabaret show into these venues. UA Sales Up In October HOLLYWOOD — United Artists has an- nounced that October was the most suc- cessful sales month in the company's his- tory. UA attributed this increase to not only increasingly successful contem- porary product, but to the sales impact of United Artists' independent distributors. Mogull Acquires 50% Simone Music NEW YORK — Ivan Mogull Music Corp has purchased 50 percent of selections controlled by Nina Simone's Ninandy Music, Bucrenlis Music, Rolls Royce Music and Bucky Music — all for his Harvard Music Inc. Mogull previously had foreign rights and now owns 50 per- cent of world rights. Mogull also acquired sub-publishing on the hit U K. single, "Barbados," by Typically Tropical on Gull Records. Polydor Mexico is releasing the original in Central and South America and Mex- ico NEW YORK — "No area in the music business is as misunderstood as the financial end, and more myths have crept out of it than any other," stated David O'Connell, president of Phonodisc Records, addressing a meeting of the B'nai B'rith music and performing arts lodge here on "Fundamentals And Myths." "I've met people who could name the call letters of every radio station across the nation but who wouldn't know the first thing about the difference between returns on sales, capital, investments or assets employed," he said. Fundamen- tals to any distribution operation, vitally important to members of the promotion field and other areas of the record busi- ness, are too often completely unfamiliar to them. How does the record industry create this situation? Here, according to O’Con- nell, is where the "myths" come in. "I've never seen a business where so many have done so much with so little. A re- cord company can be started relatively McCormick, Phillips Form October Records HOLLYWOOD — Steve McCormick and J C. Phillips have formed October Records. Jonathan Cain, whose first single "Till It's Time To Say Goodbye" is the first signing to the label which will be distributed byClaridge Records. McCormick was general manager of the Landers/Roberts label. Mums Records, and is noted for being one of the innovators of the use of the national secondary radio network He will be pre- sident of October McCormick also helped break million sellers, "Play- ground In My Mind by Clint Holmes, "Pillow Talk" by Sylvia, "Brother Louie" by Stories and "The Morning After” by Maureen McGovern Early in his career he was assistant editor to Bob Hamilton at Radio Report Phillips, vice president of October, was responsible for co-writing and co- producing the Sugarloaf hit "Green Eyed Lady." " inexpensively compared to any other business, with no necessity of attracting equity capital. You can make a lot of money on incredibly limited resources. The problem is that a one time success cannot be taken as the rule of the busi- ness. “We've seen successes in spite of ig- norance of the fundamentals, however, an organization run in the context of overall corporate planning increases the propensity for success.” Among the myths O'Connell discussed were "that a branch can operate at a loss." Why shouldn't the company owned branch be run with the same attention payed to profit as an independent dis- tribution operation? The label has only to gain from attention paid to details at all levels. Another was "timing, "that elusive component connecting artist and prod- uct to his time for success. This, accord- ing to O'Connell, was only partially true. In the case of the immense success of Elton John, MCA Records' careful coordination of all the factors relating to the production and distribution of prod- uct directly correlates to the magnitude of the artist's success. Most important of the fundamentals discussed were those involved with education. O'Connell explained that an examination of some of the small com- panies that are or have been successful would reveal that the different depart- ments were always aware of each other's problems and duties. Various interactive elements must be kept in communion if an entire company is to work efficiently. Keeping the artist informed of where he stands in the record company's overall financial picture is also vital to com- munication. sashbox/singlesreviews j 10cc (Mercury 73725) Art For Art’s Sake (4:12) l Man-Ken — BMi)(G. Gouldman, E Stewart) 10 ccing "art for art's sake/money for God's sake.” Words duplicate a melodic prom- ise of services available in the classified section of the Free Press Also could be taken for a “nyaah-nyaah” ditty aimed at the English taxman as they hover on an island just out of his greedy reach. Tongue-in-cheek; product-in-the-bank. Flip: Get It While You Can (2:54) ROY C. (Mercury 73735) i Second Time Around (3:26) (Johnson-Hammond/Unichappell — BMI) (R. Hammond) To give you an idea of what a true fine performance Roy C. surrenders here, had it been cut in 1961 the Rolling Stones would have certainly used this record as a model for a cover on one of their first albums. That might not mean a lot to someone looking fora 1975 definition, but to this reviewer it means the session recorded here is time- less. Pop, r&b. Flip: My Girl (Reggae) (3:02) SYLVERS (Capitol P-4179) Boogie Fever (3:25) (Perren-Vibes/Bull Pen — ASCAP/BMI) (K. St. Lewis, F. Perren) First release on Capitol for this nine-member family sounds destined for heavy r&b chart action Fuzz bass knocks away constantly at the bottom, beneath a variety of voices coming at you from all directions. These artists can really sing and Freddie Perren has come up with a very clean production to show their efforts in the best possible light. Flip: No info available DOLENZ, JONES, BOYCE & HART (Capitol P-4180) I Remember The Feeling (3:17) ( Father/ Eve-Lau rain — BMI/ASCAP) (T. Boyce, B Hart) Remember the Monkees? Of course you do. Well, here are two of them (Mickey Dolenz and Davey Jones) along with Tommy Boyce and Bobby Hart who wrote a string of hits back when. They're all over the place now, performing as a foursome, conjuring up nostalgia and laying out some brand-new material at the same time. Remember the feeling? Of course you will. Dealers: let the public know who these artists are. Flip: No info, available PINK FLOYD (Columbia 3-10248) Have A Cigar (3:29) (Pink Floyd — BMI) (R Waters) Analyzing the "message” behind any rock tune is risky business, especially when the cover of the album from which it was taken depicts a man bursting into flames as he shakes hands with another So, "Have A Cigar” sounds to us like a synopsis of some of the fingerpoppers who have probably tried to capitalize off the talents of the Pink Floyd group We re wrong, no doubt, but the music is the thing here: a cerebral message. Flip: No info available LEO KOTTKE (Capitol P 41 77) Power Failure (2:20) (Chrysalis — ASCAP) (G Brooker, K Reid) How many fingers can one guitar player have? And none get in the way 1 Leo de- livers his own conception of this Gary Booker/Keith Reid (Procol Harum) song in a driving acoustic manner, adding a voice which is becoming increasingly more compe- tent. Keyboard and a rhythm section round out the backup for a fine assault on the neck of Kottke s instrument Bravo, Leol Flip: No info, available HEARTSFIELD (Mercury 73742) Rocking Chair (2:40) (House Of Living — ASCAP) (F Dobbs) Strains of Dixie filter through as Heartsfield rocks away from the heart of the U S. In live performance and on record this group is a complete knockout This cut is from their third album, "Foolish Pleasures," and really demands the attention of program- mers. Great a capella harmonies as well as overall superior musicianship Pop Flip: Magic Mood (3:29) WILSON PICKETT (Wicked 8101) The Best Part Of A Man (3:07) (Sherlyn — BMI) (Reid, Clark) Wilson again shoots the air full of high excitement with an illustrated adage, "the best part of a man/is a woman/the best part of a woman/is a man.” Loose, fun, with a na-na-na hook that the dancers can na-na-na to Forgive us if we re short on com- ments, but we just want to get up and move So . Flip: How Will I Ever Know (3:10) LYNSEY DE PAUL (Mercury 73739) Sugar Shuffle (3:1 2) (ATV/Lynsey/Bluey — BMI ) (L. De Paul, Blue) Lynsey is a very hot writer in Great Britain at this point in time, and so she's earned a shot at the United States "Sugar Shuffle” is well worth that shot Cool little teasing vocal gets straight to the point, "Get some honey/forget the money/do the sugar shuffle.” The lady works with words very well and has a memorable voice. From her LP, “Love Bomb.” Flip: Love Bomb (4:46) JOHNNY MATHIS (Columbia 3-10250) Stardust (3:27) (Bel win Mills — ASCAP) (H. AM/mor stations have already begun spinning this cut which is a full minute shorter in the DJ-edit form Stock up Flip: No info, available THE WHISPERS (Soul Train JH 10430) In Love Forever (3:04) (Spectrum VII — ASCAP) (J. Hernandez) The Whispers punch out every note like the brass that open this jazzy rendition that reminds one of the late forties. A lot of scat singing over entirely groovy tracks. Not your screaming rocker but, as the lyrics and saxophone solo point out, a moving chunk of mellow. No prob getting this one on the air. Flip: No info available. ARCHIE BELL AND THE DRELLS (TSOP 84774) The Soul City Walk (3:10) (Mighty Three — BMI) (J. Whitehead, G. McFadden and V Carstarphen) The classic bounce and strut of the disco-soul genre makes telling points on this disk as Archie Bell and company put their song through some mighty diversified shift changes. Instrumentally the song is taut while the group's vocals cram a whole lot into their alloted 3:10 Flip: No info, available. The revised lyrics have to do with the wedding of the daughter of the Godfather: "I’m so glad/you all could come/to see my daughter/marry this scum,” sung to the accompaniment of Frankie The Python and his Musical Mob Ahem Flip: Stardreck (3:20) AMAZING RHYTHM ACES (ABC 12142) Amazing Grace (3:17) (Fourth Floor— ASCAP) (H R Smith) From the LP, "Stacked Deck." the ARA deal another turnaround song based on the story of a teetotal ling temperance tinkerer turned temptress, a sweet young thing who compromises her values only to leave hymn for the bottle and points south. Heavy dose of country, but will garner airplay on progressive FM as followup to "Third Rate Romance.” Flip: No info, available. BEVERLY WRIGHT (Epic 8-50162) Dreams Of Childhood (3:40) (P Morris) Beverly breaks onto the mor scene with a strong single in “Dreams Of Childhood. ” Her smooth, easy vocal has just enough edge to convey the irony behind the storyline, a grownup's daydream of the freedom of childhood What's more this young lady, who has performed all over the world, is also an excellent producer She balances fullness against sparseness very effectively. " and his hand picked cut has always been "Feel Like Makin" Love," and they're playing it down in Birm- ingham Jerry Carter has been acting PD at WTOY Roanoke since May He started working for the 1000 watt day-timer part-time while serving as a juvenile probation officer. Since he took the post programming has changed the face of the station from a basically "top 40 soul" format to 360 degrees of musical direction Now WTOY listeners can hear everything from Buddy Miles to Miles Davis; soul, jazz and top 40 crossovers including Hamilton, Joe Frank and Reynolds and the Doobie Bros. In fact. WTOY was the first in the market to play David Bowie’s “Fame." The air personality of the station has slowed down, while jingles are still used, the jocks" voices provide the major links in the music. Listeners can hear Jerry from 6 to 9; gospel from 9 to 10:30 except where interrupted three days a week by “Express Yourself,” a talk show where listeners voice their views. "Midday Magic" features Quita Allen, and is geared to the housewives who comprise the bulk of the audience at that time The afternoon drive is handled by Bobbie Knight, MD, with Ron Williams and Jimmy Soul taking over weekends. Once a month, operations manager Andy Peterson does a show examining jazz through the last four decades. Although Jerry admitted to both positive and negative feedback on the changes. WTOY is picking up the numbers of late, and is anxiously awaiting the outcome of the next ARB jess levitt/phil dimauro a SALSA BREATHER — Shown above taking a break at the Sound Factory in Hollywood are the Fama All-Stars From left to right are: Nicky Maerra, Ray Barretto, Jerry Masucci Fania Records president and co-producer of the new LP, Gene Page, LP co-producer, Johnny Pacheco, musical director, Roberto Roena, Bobby Valentin and Papo Luca. 34 November 15. 1975

. . . a series of records intended to capture important new music ..." Horizon is jazz. Horizon is a new venture from A&M Records dedicated to improvisational music and the artists who create it. Horizon will present a series of records intended to capture important new music for those interested in the remarkable and unpredictable evolution of jazz. All Horizon album covers will be gatefold and, in most cases,, will contain extensive liner notes, along with transcribed solos, a lead sheet of a selected composition, a diagram of the stereo mix of one of the selections, a graphic score of one selection (what instrument is playing when), artists' comments, and photographs. All Horizon pressings will be of the highest quality available to ensure the ultimate sonic experience. Each record will be packaged in a plastic lined inner sleeve. All Horizon albums will be available at a list price of $5.98, instead of the usual $6.98. And all tapes will be $6.98 instead of $7.98. We welcome your opinions. THAD JONES & MEL LEWIS SUITE FOR POPS SP 701 Thad Jones and Mel Lewis have been leading one of the most exciting big bands in the world for the last ten years. Their Monday night gigs at New York’s Village Vanguard are legendary. This album is Thad & Mel & Co. in a musical tribute to Louis Armstrong. Awakening JIM HALlS DAVE LIEBMAN SP 702 SWEET HANDS One of the rising stars of contempo- rary instrumental music, Dave is a former Miles Davis reed player who’s also recorded with Mahavishnu John McLaughlin and Elvin Jones. He plays all saxes and flutes and is featured with his quintet, Lookout Farm: Richie Beirach on keyboards, Badal Roy on tabla, Jeff Williams on drums, and Frank Tusa on bass. DAVE BRUBECK & SP 703 PAUL DESMOND 1975: THE DUETS Brubeck and Desmond first played duets aboard the S.S. Rotterdam Jazz Cruise earlier this year. This album marks a special moment in jazz his- tory: their first duet recording in over twenty years of performing together. It all started 2000 miles out at sea and it’s all here. Definitely a vintage set. SONNY FORTUNE AWAKENING Former Miles Davis reedman Sonny Fortune has also played and recorded with Mongo Santamaria, McCoy Tyner, and Buddy Rich. His multi- textured Horizon debut includes: Chip Lyles and Billy Hart on drums, Wayne Dockery and Reggie Workman on bass, Kenny Barron on piano, and Charles Sullivan on trumpet. SP 705 Preeminent among contemporary jazz guitarists, Jim Hall shares equal space with the two generally acknowledged masters — Django Reinhardt and Charlie Christian. This album is the best of his recent “live” performances — accompanied by Don Thompson on bass and Terry Clarke on drums. A JAZZ SERIES ON OUT* A&M RECORDS & TAPES

cashbox/album reviews pop picks BIG WHAN — Cannonball Adderley - Fantasy F 979006 - Producer: Julian Adderley, Nat Ad- derley and David Axelrod — List: 6.98 Cannonball Adderley’s final recorded effort proves a monster as his musical tribute to the legendary John Henry waxes near perfect The ease in which music and words advance the con- tinuity of the piece is a triumphant melding of media facets that works to the proverbial T. Top moments in this story set to music include "On His Bones," "Jesus Where You Now," “Grind Your Own Coffee" and "A New Star Risin." “Big Man” is an ode to John Henry but musically Big Man will always be Cannonball Adderley. CHANGE - Spanky And Our Gang - Epic PE 33580 - Producer: Spanky And Our Gang - List: 6.98 Spanky and Our Gang is a mixture of a whole lot of influences that make tagging them difficult. There's a little bit bit of rock, a touch of country and a thin slice of gospel within their musical walls. All of these bits and pieces auger well on "Change" as the group puts together a smooth series of songs perfectly fit to Spanky's unique vocal shadings. Top runs at good music include “I Wont Brand You," “I Wish Wed All Been Ready" and "Since You've Gone.” “Change” is the positive result of a group that defies being tagged. THE IMMEDIATE STORY VOLUME I - The Nice - Sire SASH 3710-2 This two record kickoff to a projected series of re-releases couldn’t have picked a finer jumping off point than The Nice This very ahead of its time band, besides fostering the early keyboard histrionics of one Keith Emerson, was the bringer of a new music that transcended the, then, predictability of the entire pop genre. Top journeys through a musical half-life include Tantalizing Maggie," "The Diamond Hard Blue Apples Of The Moon 1 ' and Bonnie K.” Progression has had many starting points The Nice was one of them. THE UNEXPLAINED - Ataraxia - RCA APL 1 1217 - Producer: Mort Garson - List: 6.98 The tarot deck. Astral projection. Cabala. All factions in orbit around the sphere of influence known as the occult. Until now a variance of the mind devoid of sound projection. With The Unexplained" by Ataraxia this world has found a voice Reams of synthesizer and distorted strings combine with haunted vocals for an over- all feel that is decidedly not of this earth Top cuts include "Astral Projection," "Wind Dance" and "Seance.” "The Unexplained” by Ataraxia is the record that goes bump in the night But it isn't real Or is it. WATER AND POWER - Water And Power - Fan- tasy F 9494 - Producer: Harvey Fuqua - List: 6.98 There are various dimensions to the easy listen. The subtle instrumental and vocal shad- ings, when they're right, point the way to an en- joyable listen. "Water And Power" shows off all the right qualities of singing projection as the group makes use of lightly tainted pop to get their soulful point across. Top laidbacks include "Ain’t No Hurt (Like The Hurt You Get),” “I Can Find A Way To Your Heart" and "If You Don't Want Me.” There's electricity in the move and electricity in the easy. Water And Power is a perfect example of the latter. RONNIE McNEIR — Ronnie McNeir — Prodigal PLP 10007 - Producer: Ronnie McNeir — List: 6.98 There's been a whole lot of physical involved in much of today's soul music The more overt phases of funk have, in many cases, lowered a curtain on the more laidback aspects of the genre. "Ronnie McNeir" shows that the mellow is still valid as a smooth mixture of McNeir's lightly-passionate vocals and polished in- strumentals make for an ease-back excursion in- to soul Top ear messages are “Baby Come Back Home,” “Nothin' But A Heartache” and "Since I Don't Have Your Love." Ronnie McNeir is through the music softly MCNEIR CRACK THE SKY - Crack The Sky - Lifesong LS 6000 - Producer: Terence Minogue, Marty Nelson and William Kirkland — List: 6.98 There comes a time in every rocker's life when the twin forks of boogie versus lush and majestic present themselves. "Crack The Sky" is a perfect example of both roads taken The band com- bines a riff-infested metallic base with an almost orchestrated aside to backing fiber with the re- sultant culmination move music suitable for a throne Lyrically the basic tones are supplement- ed by a quasi-pop esoteric approach that makes the aforementioned compositions strong story vehicles "Crack The Sky” is the best of all possi- ble musical fissures. HARMONY GRITS — Street Corner Symphony — Bang BLP 406 — Producer: Jerry Love and Michael Zager - List: 6.98 The emphasis of "Harmony Grits” is on the voice Through the chance interchange of harmonies and vocals the Street Corner Sym- phony have come up with one of the more listenable efforts in quite a long time The basic roots of soul and to the rear a few years pop mix in a gentle, undulating singing block that flows smooth through all cuts. Top voicings include "Something Funky's Goin’ On." "Someone Sweet As You” and a most professional cover of "Earth Angel ” “Harmony Grits” by Street Corner Symphony is why God gave the human mouth something to do. THIS STAR ON EVERY HEEL - Gabriel - ABC ABCD 885 - Producer: Don McKinney - List: 6.98 There is a layer of pop that is decidedly American in origin. A light country sprinkling coupled with vocals that project crystal clear. This is the avenue explored by Gabriel on "This Star On Every Heel " The group within a bouncey. upbeat vein mixes with move and ballads for an overall listen that is good to the ear Top pops include "I Wish I Were A Star,” “You Never Told Me You Loved Me” and "I See You Hiding " Gabriel s "This Star On Every Heel" is music whose roots go deep pop soil of this country. GEARS - Johnny Hammond - Milestone M 9062 - Producers: Larry and Fonce Mizell — List: 6.98 Good jazz takes you for a ride Its very being is the spawn of musical tributaries and backwashes where creative twists and turns are the rule rather than the exception. This is the world of Johnny Hammond and on "Gears" this staking out of new musical turf is enlarged and then some. Hammond's ability to combine mellow and aggressive strains shows well on all cuts with the progressions of "Tell Me What To Do.” "Shifting Gears” and "Lost On 23rd Street” standing tall. "Gears" by Johnny Hammond is music's answer to overdrive. TRIDENT - McCoy Tyner - Milestone M 9063 - Producer: Orrin Keepnews - List: 6.98 McCoy Tyner's interpretation of the mellow roots and underpinnings of jazz have long been the staples of purists and progressives alike. On Trident” his journeys to the core are supported by an alternating backup fiber that is at once sub- dued and moving Professionals in their own right add positive dimensions to Tyner's highly diversified keyboard moves while adding their own subtle touches Top cuts include “Once I Loved" and "Land Of The Lonely " "Trident" by McCoy Tyner does a whole lot of things and the best part being that they’re done wel I SECOND GENERATION - Gaylord And Holiday - Prodigal PLP 10009 - Producer: Sam Locric- chio - List: 6.98 Gaylord and Holiday are of the finest tradition of musical cabaret Within their songs is a sense of humor and staying power that has kept this duo doing what they do best for quite a long time Top cuts from this veteran singing team in- clude "To The Door Of The Sun,” “I Will Never Pass This Way Again," “Tell Me You're Mine” and "From The Vine Came The Grape " "Second Generation" is a well named album. They've been doing it that long and this record will probably keep them doing it a while longer. 28 November 22. 1 975

casfi?box/radio news Macon's WBML hits the pits: in conjunction with Capricorn Records “Peaches II” promotion, the listener who delivered the largest number of peach pits to the station was the winner of a complete Capricorn catalog The two winners (I. to r. ) , were Cheryl Croft and Al Greene: they delivered — get this — 120,000 peach pits The second prize winner received a complete Allman Brothers catalog; a total of 200,000 pits were delivered to the station. The two guys on the right, who are probably wishing they had mastered the science of alchemy, are WBML program director Ken Crook and Capricorn publicity agent Mark Pucci. The station now has enough peach pits to start its own orchard $1 ,000 worth of albums and the services of a KFRC disk jockey to emcee a dance to be held at the center's opening night. Kudos go to Waters and KFRC for think- ing of the other guy, KFRC has additionally negotiated an exclusive interview with the chairman of the board. Frank Sinatra. The interview, the first Sinatra has granted to a station in several years, will be broadcast during commuter news segments this week at 7:20 and 8:20 am on the Dr. Don Rose show. Rose is doing his show from his bed at home until his broken leg is healed While we re trolling in San Francisco Bay for coelocanth, Metromedia s KSAN-FM has been programming the best of their live broadcasts; last Nov. 8, the artists recorded live included the Wailers, Leo Sayer, the Marshall Tucker Band, Sparks, Montrose and the Hoodoo Rhythm Devils. The next day another five hours of choice Fleetwood Mac, Jimmy Buffett, Alan Price, Nils Lofgren and Robin Trower. And the next day, Randy Newman, Tower of Power, UFO, the Tubes, and Man. On the 11th Bay Area listeners got dosed with the Grateful Dead, the Allman Brothers, Peter Frampton, Stories, and marvelous Martin Mull. Upcoming is a live broadcast from the Great American Amusement Hall on Tues Nov. 18 which will feature Maria Muldaur and Geoff Muldaur. Together on the bill at least. How nice! Two weeks ago on KEZY-FM s Sunday evening “Blue Sky” segment, senatorial candidate Tom Hayden was interviewed on the air and answered, listener ques- tions. Last week Dave Forman and Caron Allen talked with Radio and Records’ album-oriented rock editor Mike Har- rison about the medium, and the three answered questions posed by I isteners. Back in the “Big D,” Steve Fromholz (who we hear will be signed to Capitol in the near future) will be doing a weekly one-hour air personality show on KFM on Sunday nights at 1 1 pm beginning Nov 23. Fromholz will interview fellow artists, sing and play when he’s into it, and will program Lone Star music and Lone Star folklore. Steve’s show will be recorded two weeks ahead of airdates, which will keep the show current while allowing him to continue his concert ap- pearances. This is another in a series of artist-oriented special programming that has earned KFM a very high regard with the artists who make Texas music. From the cornucopia of his mind comes Marc Shapiro’s Thanksgiving message “I’m not saying this record is a turkey, but I'll bet it will be on the dinner table Nov. 27 ." Stephen peeples A reminder that the last of six two-day regional radio conventions and seminars sponsored by the NAB and the RAB will be held at the Fairmont Hotel in San Francisco Nov. 20-21: additionally, the NAB will hold a separate and concurrent seminar for radio program directors on the first day. Highlights for the first day will include a luncheon address by motivationalist Hugh Finnerty; the luncheon address on the final day will be delivered by FCC commissioner Benjamin L. Hooks. Earth News' Jeff Hillery indicated that the Univ. of Cal at Los Angeles (UCLA) and the Umv. of Wisconsin at Madison have received the best response for the broadcasts. The December issue of Playboy invites radio listeners to participate in this year's Playboy Music Poll. The poll is divided into jazz, rock, r&b and c&w categories, and votes will be taken for top male and female vocalists, groups, composers and instrumentalists. The in- troduction of the poll to the radio listen- ing public will be kicked off by the Playboy Music Poll Giveaway; with the cooperation of Superscope/Marantz, a series of prize packages including Superscope radios and Marantz sound equipment will be offered. Listeners can procure ballots from selected retailers and after filling them out, ballots sent to participating radio stations in 25 major markets will make the listener eligible for daily and grand prize drawings. The re- sults will be published in Playboy next spring. The KWST broadcast of Willie Nelson s opening show at the Troubadour last Thurs night was extremely well- received; several folks at our table the next evening said they had heard the broadcast the evening before and de- cided to check out “Shotgun'' Willie for themselves. Four more new Nelson con- verts Roger Miller and Mac Davis joined Willie and Jody Payne and the Willie Nelson Band for a few numbers onstage. In what program director Ron Martin describes as a “management decision." KGBS is no longer the 8-midnight hutch for progressive country disk jockey Jimmy Rabbitt. When asked if the station would continue to program the pro- gressive spectrum between traditional country and country/rock, Martin em- phatically affirmed. Rabbitt has no hard feelings: "I guess they got tired of listen- ing to my shows to see if I said the things some listeners have accused me of say- ing The complaints were inaccurate, but it takes a lot of valuable time to check out the complaints." Rabbitt, who will appear at the Palomino later this month, went on to say that he hoped KGBS would "con- tinue to program that kind of music. I'm one guy; the music is a lot bigger than any one guy Michael Hunter will be behind the mike from 7-midnight, followed by Nancy Plum, who moves from weekender to keeper of the KGBS graveyard. In addition to the news, there will be AUSTIN - A segment of the "Austin City Limits" television show featuring Bob Wills' Original Texas Playboys and Asleep At The Wheel will be telecast on the Public Broadcasting System late in January The show was taped in Austin recently and marked the first time in public appearance for the Playboys since the death of Bob Wills last May As a re- sult of the overwhelming response by the relatively young audience at the tap- ing, a series of concert dates will be forthcoming for the band which backed Wills, who is recognized as the patriarch of western swing The soon-to-return Playboys have all backed Bob Wills at various points in the long and legendary life of the first and primary Texas swing band organized by Wills in the early 1930s; the current band includes several of the original members. Pianist Al Stricklin, who joined the Texas Playboys in Sept. 1935, stated that the Austin City Limits taping was “the first time in 30 years we had all played together The only rehearsing was by the fiddle players and a guitar to work out who was going to play which harmony part, but we all knew the music. mashboxR&Bnewsreport r&h ingredients It’s been awhile for ex-Temptation David Ruffin to have a monster, but the man with the crystal high voice has the hottest record out at the moment. “Walk Away From Love” is probably the most refreshing tune of the year and even bigger than the thrilla from Manila. David was in town this week and yours truly had the opportunity to go over and rap with the man who has had quite a singing career. David has been singing his whole life. "Singing is everything to me. It’s really a thrill to have a hit again and I'm grateful to Van McCoy for helping me make my LP 'Who I Am.’ I feel it is a great change and progression in my music and sound.” When I asked David about the high note in the bridge where his voice almost pops, he laughed. “Yeah, it was a high note, but the feeling was so natural that Van and I decided to leave it that way. I feel it just adds to the emotion of the tune." A little side-note about David is that when he first came to Detroit he used to sing in a trio with a couple of guys — Marvin Gaye and Lament Dozier. David taped American Bandstand and Rock Concert last week. Next month he will be on tour along with Van McCoy, Melba Moore and Faith, Hope and Charity — all on the same bill. Should be some show . . . Disco music is really starting to pop on through with “Fly, Robin, Fly" by the Silver Convention, #1 on the Cash Box charts “That's The Way I Like It,” by K.C. and the Sunshine Band is holding down the #2 slot ... Do the double bump. . . . It's been a while but Major Harris has just released a new single entitled "I Got Over Love,” which should continue to make the Major a major star. This is a great follow-up to "Love Won't Let Me Wait.” . . . Also heard from a reliable source that the Major, along with Blue Magic and Margie Joseph, will be doing a live LP at the Latin Casino sometime the first part of next year It will be billed as the 3M Show . Blue Magic and Margie Joseph are now in Philadelphia finishing up tracks for their upcoming Blue Magic/Margie Joseph LP . A couple of lovely ladies have new releases out that will surely dazzle everybody out there. Dionne Warwick’s new LP "Track Of The Cat," produced by Thom Bell for Warners is out and it’s a delightful way to spend a lazy evening listening to it Ann Peebles’ new LP “Come To Mama,” on London is another killer. . . . The Philly explosion is coming like a whirlwind. The new O’Jays’ "Family Reunion” and MFSB’s “Philadelphia Freedom” LPs are sensational cut for cut This week more monsters are on the way with the release of "Dance Your Troubles Away” by Archie Bell and the Drells, "Wake-up Everybody," by Harold Melvin and the Bluenotes and one to really watch is “Happy About The Whole Thing,” by Dede Sharp Gamble. Also Columbia is releasing the long-awaited Earth, Wind & Fire LP “Gratitude ” Edward Windsor Wright has announced the exclusive worldwide press representa- tion for Philly Groove/Warner Bros. Records and their artists The First Choice, Delfonics, Quickest Way Out and 1-Band and the Bicentennial poet Jean Claude Toran. Ramsey Lewis has also re-signed with the agency for press representation . Gil Scott-Heron and the Midnight Band are making some personnel changes. Leaving the group are Eddie Adenola, Charlie Saunders, Victor Brown and O.D. Bob Adams. The new replacements are Tony Duncanson on percussion and Reggie Brisbane on drums. Brian Jackson, leader of the Midnight Band will now be carrying some of the vocal load with Gil. If you haven't heard it yet their latest LP “From South Africa to South Carolina,” you're missing something in your life Sister Sledge with "Love Has Found Me” on the charts will be doing a gig in Chicago during their Thanksgiving vacation from school Mickey Stevenson, manageroffhe Infernal Blues Machine, has just negoiated adeal for the group with Brut Productions and Atlas Film Distributors in conjunction with London Records for the group to do the soundtrack for the forthcoming film “Adios Amigo." The stars of the film will be Fred Williamson and Richard Pryor A&M recording artists Shades of Blue were honored recently when they were recipients of The Caribbean Community Award, citing them for their musical and cultural contribu- tions to the westside community of Los Angeles. The ladies, former background singers for Aretha Franklin, are Patricia Mitchell, Margaret Branch and Verlena Rogers. They have just released a new single entitled "Waiting For The Last Goodbye," which was produced by "Dynomite" Tony Camillo. Tony has been a busy guy lately as he produced two other new singles currently out, "Love Explosion” by Bazuka on A&M and "Higher And Higher" by Martha Reeves on Arista Johnny “Guitar” Watson is at the West German Music Festival in Berlin while his new single on Fantasy "It's Too Late,” is rocketing up the charts. It s a very funky smooth single . Even though a new Marvin Gaye LP won't be out for awhile, Marvin is out on the concert circuit. He will be in Tempe, Arizona next week doing a show along with George Carlin . Warner Brothers’ recording artist Jimmy Cliff is in town taping Rock Concert. Beginning Nov. 19 the man from "The Harder They Come," will be at the Roxy Theater . The Impressions are knocking 'em dead back east while on tour. “Same Thing It Took" is still a heavy duty favorite The guys' next single release will be "Lovin' Power." . Pops Staple went into the hospital for surgery for some growths in his throat. Fortunately they were benign. Pops is resting well, however the group will not be appearing for the rest of the year. Their latest single and LP, "Let's Do It Again" is the year-end smash We at Cash Box hope Pops is on his feet very soon. HERE’S OLE RAYS! Doing It With "A Helluva Thing" The Flip Side Blues is "Tough Competition" Got it Get it Already hitbound in: Texas Louisiana Arkansas Kansas Missouri Chicago NOW RELEASED ON PROWLIN’ RECORD LABEL 2225 W Washington Blvd. Los Angeles, California 90018 Mornay To Handle Manticore Promo HOLLYWOOD — Lester J Mornay & As- sociates have been retained by Man- ticore Records, Ltd. to handle national publicity and public relations for their re- cording artists Thee Image, Little Richard and Maxayn. Lester Mornay & Associates will be responsible for creating and implement- ing a national publicity campaign in con- nection with the release of new product and personal appearance tours in behalf of the artists. A FOXY FOURSOME — Shown above are Sister Sledge taking a breather from touring by walking in a Philadelphia park. The girls are currently back in school watching their latest single "Love Has Found Me,” penned by Kathi, climb up the charts. Mercury Records is making the move into the world of reggae with some new re- leases. Roy C. has a new LP entitled "Something Nice." Other reggae LPs scheduled for a December release are Byron Lee and the Dragonaires with "Disco Reggae." Greyhound with “Leave The Reggae To Us," and G.T. Moore with “G.T Moore.” With "Good Old Fashioned Lovin' " lookin’ to be a big hit Brenda Lee Eager will be out working to do it live. The gal will be doing the Playboy Club in L A Nov. 21-22 and 28-29. Currently Brenda is in the studios laying some tracks for her next single. . . . David Bowie taped Soul Train over the weekend along with RCA s Faith, Hope and Charity. No airdate has been set. David’s new single is being released this week and rumor has it that it’s even badder' than “Fame." Gary Gotham, my New York disco spy, had to make an emergency phone call here because all our lines were tied up. He was excited He couldn't wait to tell me about Bobby Hebb's latest single "Sunny 76." This is the same smash tune of the past updat- ed into the disco mold and the record is creating a sensation in New York. The flip side is “Sunny” (Disco). “Find My Way," a new single released by Cecil Holmes’ Chocolate City Records has had some changes made. The group that recorded it was originally known as the Players. They have changed their name and are known as Cameo Freddy North on Nashboro Records is releasing a new single entitled “Cuss The Wind.” It's a sleeper. The hottest thing happening on the streets these days is about singer Kellee Patterson. Her recent spread in Black Stars has created quite a commotion and the girl is presently being pursued by several large companies for her John Hancock on a recording deal. . . . THUNDER ON HAVEN — Haven recording artist Margo Thunder has a new single out entitled “Don't You Have Any Love In Your Heart." From left to right are: Harvey Stein and Bert DeCoteaux her producers, Margo and Matt Parson, national r&b pro- motion and sales director. Heard from a reliable source that Don Cornelius has asked the Miracles to pen some tunes for his Soul Train label. Don has been totally knocked out by the group's latest LP and single “City Of Angels” and "Love Machine.” . . . Alex Hodges, president of the Paragon Agency has signed legendary blues performer Muddy Waters. Born McKinley Morganfield, in Rolling Park Mississippi, Muddy is still active in the business and he recently penned “Can't Lose What You Never Had,” on the latest Allman Brothers Band LP "Win, Lose Or Draw ”. . . . Bumps Doogan, my L A. man on the scene can't stop bumping after he heard "Oh No, Not My Baby.” by De Blanc on Arista Records. "The tune really lays a heavy groove on you.” . . Hodges James & Smith took time off from rehearsing their play and opened at the ETC Club in Los Angeles last week. The girls looked and sounded sensational during their show. Some of the celebs watching the sassy lassies doin' their thing included Jim Brown, Freda Payne, The People’s Choice and Harry Williams, Jr. of Bloodstone. Harry just returned from their debut in Detroit on Halloween. He said the night was really crazy as the movie “Train Ride To Hollywood,” was being pre- miered at two different theatres and the group performed live before each of the screenings. "They had us up in a helicopter to get us to both places and the ride was so shakey that I felt that I was riding on a broom,” said Harry as he laughed. Speaking of the People’s Choice, the group has been in town and the guys came up to the Cash Box offices to rap and say hel lo. The People's Choice is no new group as the the three original members have been doin’ it together for ten years. Frank Brounson, one of the original men said it had been a long hard climb with a lot of bologna between records "but now that we're with Leon and Kenny we’re tickled pink.” The other guys in the group include Dave Thompson, Rodger Andrews, Guy Fisk, Sam Peak and Darnell Jordon. The group did have some minor successes before “Do It Any Way You Wanna." Back in 1971 the guys' recorded "I Likes To Do It,” on the Filet of Soul label. This was followed by "Wootie-To Woo-Woo.” In 1973 they signed with TSOP. Their first single with them was “Party Is A Groovey Thing," and now they are enjoy- ing their first number one smash. The guys said they really dig the funky disco stuff that they are doing, because being solid musicians they enjoy being able to hold that skintight groove. “Even though the riff we're using is a simple one,” Sam Peak said, “it's not that easy being able to keep it tight in the pocket.” The group was in town tap- ing some TV, shows including Dick Clark's American Bandstand. Frank, who by the way, says he's a natural for TV said the group's next single will be “Nursery Rhymes.” The People's Choice is a group of six guys that looks to be right on target for a long time to come, that's soul. . jess levitt •1.6 November 22, 1975

Bobby Elliot of KNOK believes a combination of things go into the making of a top- notch jock. One of the most important things Bobby said was for the jock to be level- headed "A good voice is important but more importantly the guy or gal has to be able to relate with me We don’t have to be super-tight, however, we have to be able to re- late with one another. Secondly, the jock has to have a good knowledge of music. He has to play records not for himself, but be able to play records that work well within our format concept. Thirdly, the jock should be outgoing, have a varied background and have good mechanical production skills. And finally, have that one natural quali- ty, which is talent " Joe Fischer at WCKO feels that a jock should have a strong radio background and have attended the best radio school possible. His knowledge of music must be strong and Joe likes a guy to have been in a high school band or chorus so he has a close re- lationship with music. Another important aspect Joe feels important is that the jock must be all business when he is on the air. "Radio is a business and the jock has to totally understand the business end of it." Another area Joe looks at is if the jock is community minded "Top 40 jocks are not usually into the community; however, black jocks must be into the people, their problems and surroundings." Joe said that at WCKO he and his guys come up with ideas for community involvement and take them to the boss for approval. Joe looks for a jock that understands the human element in people, because he feels that jocks must know how to talk with their audience and know how to present what they are talking about. He wants a guy who acts pro- fessional so he doesn’t have to worry about what the guy does. "When the jock has an attitude like this, it is very easy for his personality to come through.” Al Parker, program director at WUFO in Buffalo, feels first that the jock must be creative. “There’s too many guys that steal from one another. I look for originality in my people. Second, they must love music, and they must love radio. Also they must maintain a business attitude when they are working, even though they are rapping and spinning records. A good jock to me thinks radio 24 hours a day. He is constantly listening and going out to clubs, record stores and discos looking for that reaction that certain records cause. Another area I feel strongly about is how the jock's personality comes through and how he can add it to the programming of his show to get the best response. Some guys can ad-lib under any situation and others can’t and in radio you cannot be at a loss for words. You have to feel it and have to believe in yourself and yourability." Dick Green, pd at WSOK in Savannah, believes that the most important thing for a jock is dedication to his craft. He has to know everything, from records to the control room, and be able to handle any situation that arises. If there is a foul-up he must be able to adjust and make the transition smoothly. “Another thing is that he must be able to announce. Anybody can spin records. The jock cannot play music that just suits himself, but must play music for his audience." Also Dick commented that the jock's voice must be air worthy. It has to be a pleasant melodious voice. And finally he must master the equipment he uses in his everyday duties.” Bob Moore, pd at KDKO in Denver, believes first that the jock must be able to com- municate, understand communication and also have a good knowledge of music. He added that the jock must not be an ego-tripper. "The jock of today is not a rapper, but more a communicator; he must be informed and involved in the community so he is better able to communicate with that audience. I look for a guy who can do the news as well as spin records, the total all-around announcer He must have a good com- mand of the English language and finally, have an image that relates to the station and the community." Rob Singleton at KRE-FM in Berkeley looks for a jock who is a thinker and has a good personality. "He should have a sense of humor and a good wit. His knowledge of music must be first-rate. I know every jock has favorite music but it has to be put together in a well-balanced format. I also look for a guy that doesn't jive on the air I like a straightforward and honest individual A good voice is important; however, I look for a guy with a natural sounding voice and one that doesn’t scream, shout or rave. I like my guys to be involved with the community and interested in total involve- ment rather than just doing their thing. I like dedicated people, who are dedicated to what they are doing. David Darnell, WDIA, Memphis — " I would look for someone with a "contemporary" sound. He should be able to work in the areas of both pop and r&b radio. Our station has changed quite a bit recently, and we re operating in a market where it’s necessary to compete with top 40 radio, so we’ve developed a sort of "Black 40" sound " Dave says WDIA is getting away from “the old rapping style," playing more music, necessitating a fast delivery He was quick to mention, however, that going overboard in the speed dept is strictly to be avoided. continued on pg . so NOW AVAILABLE!
